claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in harsh environments is governed by a refined, passivating near-surface microstructure produced by microalloying.
Low-level boron addition to AlCoCrFeNiMoTiBx promotes in situ formation of fine TiB2 particles.
Low-level boron addition significantly refines the near-surface grain structure.
The undoped AlCoCrFeNiMo-based baseline has a conventional multiphase or coarse-grained microstructure.
Fine TiB2 precipitates act as barriers to crack initiation.
Fine precipitates and refined grain boundaries increase hardness and impede plastic deformation during sliding.
The increased hardness and impeded plastic deformation reduce wear rate.
Grain refinement and TiB2 precipitates help sustain a stable passive film during mechanical deformation.
The refined microstructure minimizes corrosion-initiation defect sites and promotes a dense, chemically uniform passive oxide film.
Stabilization of the passive oxide film reduces corrosion.
Relative to an undoped baseline, the boron-microalloyed sample will have a lower wear rate.
Relative to an undoped baseline, the boron-microalloyed sample will have a lower friction coefficient.
Relative to an undoped baseline, the boron-microalloyed sample will have a lower corrosion current density.
Tribocorrosion degradation of the microalloyed sample will be less severe than the sum of isolated wear and corrosion effects observed in the baseline.
The predicted benefit holds only within an optimized boron concentration range that produces fine TiB2 and grain refinement.
A boron level that is too low will not appreciably alter the microstructure.
Excessive boron will cause precipitate agglomeration and defects, eliminating the wear-corrosion benefit.
Prior studies report that alloying or microalloying can improve separately measured wear-related and corrosion-related performance.
The quantitative interaction between wear and corrosion under coupled degradation remains uncertain and may depend on processing and service conditions.

contradictions.description: The modified composition AlCoCrFeNiMoTiBx adds Ti as well as B relative to the stated AlCoCrFeNiMo baseline, whereas the experiment describes the samples as differing only in boron and otherwise having nearly identical composition. This would confound the proposed boron-only comparison.

The outcome predicts coupled degradation relative to the sum of isolated wear and corrosion effects, but the experiment specifies only simultaneous exposure and does not explicitly include the isolated wear-only and corrosion-only tests needed to evaluate that prediction.
